newsitem.title: UK: UK accepts Stagecoach moves on bus services.
newsitem.headline: UK accepts Stagecoach moves on bus services.

text.p: The UK government said it had accepted undertakings from bus operator Stagecoach Holdings Plc to remedy the adverse effects on competition of some of its activities in the north of England.

Corporate and consumer affairs minister John Taylor said Stagecoach had followed recommendations from Britain's competition watchdog the Monopolies and Mergers Commission to remedy adverse effects of price cuts on services in the north east of England.
The MMC had found that Stagecoach's price cuts were likely to damage competition in the longer term.
Taylor said Stagecoach's actions would limit its ability to retaliate against both new operators entering the market and existing competitors.

For example, Taylor said, if Stagecoach cut prices to a level below its competitors on a particular route and the competitors had to withdraw the service, Stagecoach would have to maintain its prices in real terms on that route for three years.
"I am satisfied that these undertakings remedy the adverse effects identified by the MMC," he said.
The MMC published its report on August 3 1995. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
